albums.description: This was the Summer of my first long bicycle tour.  I started in Portland, Oregon and worked my way up the coast to the Olympic Peninsula then up to Port Townsend, Washington.  I crossed over into Canada at Victoria, British Columbia and was joined by a friend.  We bicycled up the East Coast of Vancouver Island, took a passenger ferry to Lasqueti Island, hitched a boat ride to a beach on Texada Island, caught a passenger ferry to Powell River on the Sunshine Coast and biked up to Lund.  From there we worked our way down to Vancouver and closed the loop back in Victoria.  I went on by myself to Vancouver in search of a public park I had read about in The Starship And The Canoe by Kenneth Brower.  The book mentioned Belcarra Park, a Vancouver city park full of squatters (this was in the '70s) and I thought I'd go take a look.  This forced me to bike through Vancouver which I didn't want to do.  I'm glad I did though as I met up with a lot of interesting people and had some great bike adventures.  By the way, in 2013 the squatters were still in Belcarra Park!  With my new friends from Vancouver, we took a ferry to Nanaimo on Vancouver Island and biked to Ucluelet and Tofina.  It was an amazing bike tour.
albums.title: Bicycle Trip Summer 2013

albums.description:
I was lucky enough to attend a class by Doug "Digger" Crist at Winter Count 2016.  He is an expert tanner and a very awesome human being.  The essentials steps that he led us through were: 1. Scraping the fat/meat pieces from the "membrane" side of the hide.  2.  Soaking in a light lye solution (alternatively, ash can be used) to help with the hair and grain removal.  3. Scraping of the hair side to remove hair and the top grain.  This was seriously hard work.  Push harder.  4. Soak thoroughly to get the internal pH neutralized.  5.  Re-scrape the membrane side.  6. Make brain solution and thoroughly soak and squish this solution through the hide.  7.  Stretch and work hide thoroughly.  Push harder.  8.  Smoke the hide.  Sound about right?

The last pictures are from Lynx Vilden's class on making something with a hide.  Her stitch demo piece is impressive.
albums.title: Brain Tanning Dear Hide - Winter Count Festival 2016

In July and August of 2015 we took two identical Pacific Loons up from Port Townsend Washington through the San Juan Islands and into Canada's Gulf Islands.  We camped in the boats at anchor and on land.  They are pretty ideal row touring boats and provide a lot of comfort and flexibility compared to touring in kayaks.  I was able to build this design in 6 days and I have been using it actively for a year now. albums.description:
My grandmother Ruth Laughlin passed away in January 2018. She was a wonderful human being and a major influence on my life. She was witty, pretty harsh (when she needed to be) and damn smart. She took my brother Christopher and I all over, from dragging us through every NYC museum, to introducing us to the West coast and around England with our grandfather, Bill. While we were in England she let Chris (probably 12) and I (probably 14) go to Calais, France on the hovercraft by ourselves! Yikes. We spent a lot of school holidays and sick days making pottery with her in her basement studio. She was a great sculptor (her house was filled with miniature naked ladies) and artist in general. She was a huge fan of being constructive and during summers in her Idaho camp, Chris and I were constantly working on projects that she encouraged: small boats, beading projects, weaving, painting, model making, chipmunk training, and later construction projects around the camp. She valued creativity and industriousness. I miss Ruth and my grandfather, Bill, big time.

Stephanie and I were lucky to be able to be with Ruth, Sara, Christopher, Hannah, Esther, Bruce and Claudia last week to spend a few last days with her in Providence. In her last hours, a beautiful immense swirling mass of crows formed outside her window. It was one more unusual adventure with Ruth.
albums.title: Ruth

Ok, so it wasn't much of a mystery, but we found a beautiful book about the St. Lawrence on the shelf in the exotic old Providence Athenaeum and it had a picture of an engraved dog that Steph recognized.  We were heading to Québec City in a few days after finding the book, so we headed out to find the dog.  It turns out to be the subject of a lot of stories and is quite famous and easy to find near the historic downtown of Québec City.

Here is some of the history of the Golden Dog:  www.ameriquefrancaise.org/en/article-590/The_Golden_Dog.html
